areas.why: Beachfront hotels near the Port Olímpic offer sea views, pools and easy beach access, ideal for those who want a resort feel within the city.

themes.anniversary: Barcelona marks an anniversary best through food and architecture. Base yourselves on Passeig de Gràcia in a suite with a terrace facing the Modernista facades, and book a tasting menu at one of the city's celebrated creative Catalan restaurants. Take a private guided visit of the Sagrada Família early, catch a performance at the Palau de la Música Catalana, and spend an evening sailing along the coast at sunset before a late dinner, Spanish-style, well after ten.
themes.ultra: Barcelona's most coveted stays are penthouse suites with private rooftop pools above the Eixample and seafront duplexes looking straight out over the Mediterranean, a few with sightlines to the spires of the Sagrada Família. Service extends to private chefs, yacht charters from Port Vell and guided private access at Gaudí landmarks. Outdoor space is the real differentiator here, so prioritize top-floor suites where the terrace rivals the living room in size.

new-york.overview: New York's luxury is all about access and energy: suites high above Central Park, a doorman who knows your name, and a short walk to Broadway, Fifth Avenue and the world's great museums. The city's best hotels range from storied grand dames on the Upper East Side to sleek downtown towers, all set against one of the most dynamic dining scenes anywhere.
new-york.bestTime: September through November brings crisp weather and autumn color in Central Park, while April through June offers mild days and blooming parks. December is cold but festive, with holiday windows and lights; July and August can be hot and humid.

areas.name: Midtown and Central Park South
areas.why: Steps from Central Park, Fifth Avenue and Broadway, this is the classic base for first-time visitors and anyone who wants iconic park and skyline views.

areas.name: Upper East Side
areas.why: Elegant and residential, near the Metropolitan Museum of Art and Madison Avenue boutiques, it suits travelers who want old-money calm and gracious townhouse streets.

areas.name: Tribeca and SoHo
areas.why: Downtown's former warehouse districts now hold design-led hotels, galleries and celebrated restaurants, a good fit for travelers who want a cooler, neighborhood feel.

themes.anniversary: New York turns an anniversary into an event. Book a suite with Central Park views at a landmark hotel near Fifth Avenue, start with Champagne as the skyline lights up, and reserve a tasting menu at one of the city's acclaimed fine-dining rooms. A night at the Metropolitan Opera or a Broadway premiere, a horse-drawn carriage ride or a private stroll through the park, and a late-night jazz club in the Village give the celebration that only-in-New-York quality.
themes.ultra: New York's most exceptional suites are penthouses in all but name: wraparound terraces forty or more floors up, Central Park spread out below, private gyms, chef's kitchens and grand pianos in the living room. Butlers and chauffeured cars come with the territory, and well-connected concierges can secure courtside seats, sold-out tables or a private after-hours gallery viewing. Height and silence are the true currency, and the towers around Central Park and the Upper East Side's discreet townhouse suites deliver both.

honolulu.overview: Oahu combines the energy of Waikiki with the island's quieter shores. Luxury here means oceanfront suites facing Diamond Head, beachfront resorts on the calm lagoons of the leeward coast, and the gracious aloha style of Hawaiian hospitality. It suits travelers who want world-class dining, surfing, hiking and Pearl Harbor history alongside time on the sand.
honolulu.bestTime: Oahu is warm year-round, with the drier, sunnier months running roughly from April through October. Spring and fall are typically quieter and good value, while winter brings occasional showers and big surf to the North Shore.

areas.name: Waikiki
areas.why: Honolulu's famous beachfront is the heart of Oahu's hotel scene, with Diamond Head views, high-end shopping and restaurants, ideal for those who want energy and convenience.

areas.name: Kahala
areas.why: Just east of Diamond Head, this exclusive residential enclave offers a quiet beach and stately estates, perfect for travelers seeking calm within easy reach of Waikiki.

areas.name: Ko Olina
areas.why: On Oahu's sunny west coast, this resort area features calm man-made lagoons and golf, a good choice for families and couples who want a self-contained resort feel.

themes.honeymoon: For a honeymoon on Oahu, balance Waikiki's buzz with seclusion. Choose an oceanfront suite with a lanai facing Diamond Head, or retreat to a quieter beachfront resort in Kahala or Ko Olina. Book a sunset catamaran sail off Waikiki, hike to the Diamond Head summit at dawn, and drive the windward coast to Lanikai and Kailua beaches. A private helicopter tour over the island's waterfalls and green ridges makes an unforgettable shared memory.
themes.anniversary: Celebrating an anniversary on Oahu, look to Waikiki's historic beachfront hotels, where the legacy of old Hawaii lingers in grand lobbies and oceanfront verandas. Book a suite with views across the water to Diamond Head and plan a chef's tasting menu showcasing Hawaiian ingredients. Spend a day at the North Shore, visit Pearl Harbor for reflection, and end with a mai tai at sunset as the conch shell sounds and torches are lit along the beach.
themes.golf: Oahu has a serious golf scene for an island its size. Waialae Country Club, a private club in Kahala, is a longtime PGA Tour host, while Ko Olina Golf Club on the sunny west coast offers resort golf with water features and ocean breezes. Elsewhere, courses on the windward side play beneath the fluted green cliffs of the Koolau Range. Base yourself in Ko Olina or Kahala for a golf-focused stay, and book morning tee times before the trade winds pick up.
themes.ultra: Oahu's most exclusive stays fall into two camps: presidential suites high above Waikiki with views sweeping from Diamond Head along the whole curve of the beach, and private beachfront villas on the quieter shores of Kahala and Ko Olina. Butlers, in-villa chefs and helicopter sightseeing are arranged on request, as are private surf lessons with local watermen and charter boats for snorkeling or whale watching in winter. The villas, in particular, offer the scale of a private estate with full hotel service.

cancun.overview: Cancun and the Riviera Maya pair turquoise Caribbean water and powdery white sand with Mayan ruins, jungle cenotes and some of Mexico's most lavish resorts. Luxury here leans toward the all-suite resort: private plunge pools, oceanfront villas, butler service and spas built around Mayan rituals. It suits travelers who want beach seclusion with culture and adventure close by.
cancun.bestTime: December through April is the dry season, with sunshine, low humidity and comfortable temperatures. Summer is hot and humid, and the Atlantic hurricane season runs from June through November, with the highest risk typically from August through October.

areas.name: Cancun Hotel Zone
areas.why: A long strip of beachfront between the Caribbean and the Nichupté Lagoon, it offers the area's liveliest dining and nightlife, ideal for travelers who want energy and convenience.

areas.name: Playa Mujeres and Costa Mujeres
areas.why: North of the city, this quieter stretch of coast features newer, sprawling resorts and calm water, suited to couples and families who want seclusion close to the airport.

areas.name: Riviera Maya
areas.why: The coast south toward Playa del Carmen and Tulum mixes gated luxury resort communities, cenotes and Mayan ruins, perfect for travelers who want nature, culture and space.

themes.honeymoon: For a honeymoon, the Riviera Maya's private villas are the draw: suites with their own plunge pools, outdoor showers and hammocks strung over jungle or beachfront. Choose a secluded resort between Playa del Carmen and Tulum, and spend days swimming in cenotes, snorkeling the reef and exploring the clifftop ruins at Tulum. Book a private dinner on the beach under the stars, and consider a couples' temazcal, a traditional Mayan sweat-lodge ceremony that many spas offer.
themes.anniversary: For an anniversary on the Mexican Caribbean, look to the grandest oceanfront suites in the Hotel Zone or Playa Mujeres, with sweeping terraces over the turquoise water. Celebrate with a chef's tasting menu built on Yucatecan flavors such as achiote and sour orange, charter a private yacht to Isla Mujeres for lunch and snorkeling, and make the day trip inland to the great Mayan city of Chichén Itzá. Back at the resort, a mezcal tasting at sunset is a fitting toast.
themes.golf: The Riviera Maya has become one of Mexico's golf hubs. El Camaleón at Mayakoba, designed by Greg Norman, has hosted the PGA Tour and weaves through mangroves, jungle and limestone canals to the sea. Other courses in Playa del Carmen and Puerto Aventuras offer jungle and oceanside layouts. Base yourself between Cancun and Playa del Carmen to reach several courses easily, and tee off early to beat the midday heat.
themes.wellness: Wellness in the Riviera Maya draws on the region's Mayan heritage and its natural setting. Resort spas here often feature cenote-inspired hydrotherapy circuits, temazcal sweat-lodge ceremonies led by local practitioners and treatments using native ingredients like cacao, honey and copal. Pair them with sunrise yoga on the beach, swims in clear freshwater cenotes and clean, local cuisine. Choose a resort set in jungle or along a quiet coastal stretch for a true reset.
themes.ultra: The Mexican Caribbean's highest tier is the multi-bedroom villa: a private compound with its own infinity pool, chef and butler, often stepping directly onto the sand or set deep in jungle along the Riviera Maya. Many top resorts sit inside gated estates with private beach clubs, so the seclusion is built in. Yacht charters, helicopter transfers from Cancun airport and guided visits to Mayan sites ahead of the day-trippers are routine requests at this level.

los-cabos.overview: At the southern tip of the Baja California peninsula, where the desert meets the Sea of Cortez and the Pacific, Los Cabos delivers a distinctive mix of rugged landscapes, golf, sportfishing and polished resort luxury. Its top properties feature cliffside villas, infinity pools and spas facing the dramatic coastline, appealing to travelers who want sun, scenery and outdoor adventure.
los-cabos.bestTime: November through April is the most pleasant time, with warm, dry days and cooler evenings; it also coincides with humpback whale season, roughly December through March. Summers are hot and humid, and the Pacific hurricane season runs from roughly June through November.

areas.name: Cabo San Lucas
areas.why: The lively marina town near the famous rock arch at Land's End is the base for sportfishing, boating and nightlife, ideal for those who want energy and easy access to the water.

areas.name: The Tourist Corridor
areas.why: The coastal stretch between Cabo San Lucas and San José del Cabo holds many of the region's top resorts and golf courses, perfect for travelers who want seclusion and space.

areas.name: San José del Cabo
areas.why: The quieter colonial town features art galleries and a charming historic center, suited to those who want culture, dining and a more relaxed pace.

themes.honeymoon: Los Cabos suits honeymooners who want romance with a sense of adventure. Book a cliffside villa with a private plunge pool on the Tourist Corridor, overlooking the Sea of Cortez. Take a private sunset sail around the arch at Land's End, swim and snorkel in the protected bays such as Santa Maria and Chileno, and spend an afternoon in the art galleries of San José del Cabo. Ask for a private beach dinner, and keep in mind that many beaches here are too rough for swimming.
themes.anniversary: For an anniversary, Los Cabos offers drama and fine dining. Choose a resort suite with a terrace overlooking the sea and celebrate with a chef's tasting menu showcasing Baja's seafood, wines from the Valle de Guadalupe and the region's farm-to-table produce. Spend a morning whale watching in season, take a sunset cruise past the arch at Land's End, and arrange a private dinner on the beach or among the desert cacti as the sky turns pink.
themes.golf: Los Cabos is one of the world's great golf destinations, with courses designed by major names set between desert and sea. Cabo del Sol, Quivira and Diamante are among the most celebrated, offering dramatic ocean holes and sweeping desert terrain. Base yourself on the Tourist Corridor for easy access to the region's top courses, and plan rounds for the cooler, drier months from November through April.
themes.wellness: Wellness in Los Cabos draws on the stark beauty of the desert and the sea. The region's resort spas often blend Mexican botanicals, ocean-view treatment rooms and outdoor hydrotherapy, with sunrise yoga facing the Sea of Cortez. Pair spa days with desert hikes, horseback rides along the beach and fresh, local cuisine. Choose a resort on the quieter stretches of the Tourist Corridor or near San José del Cabo for a restorative stay.
themes.ultra: In Los Cabos, the most rarefied stays are sprawling villas cut into the clifftops, with infinity pools that seem to hover over the surf, desert gardens and dedicated staff. Several elite resorts wrap their villas in private residential enclaves, so guests rarely encounter anyone outside their party. A private sportfishing boat out of the Cabo San Lucas marina, in-villa spa treatments and a private chef cooking the morning's catch are the kind of requests the best properties handle effortlessly.

sydney.overview: Sydney offers big-city sophistication framed by one of the world's most beautiful harbors. Luxury here means suites with views of the Sydney Opera House and Harbour Bridge, waterfront dining with world-class seafood and Australian wines, and easy access to the beaches of the eastern suburbs. It appeals to travelers who want an outdoor lifestyle with the culture and polish of a global city.
sydney.bestTime: September through November and March through May offer mild, sunny weather ideal for exploring the harbor and beaches. December through February is summer, hot and busy, while June through August is cooler but often bright and clear.

areas.name: The Rocks and Circular Quay
areas.why: The historic harborfront district beside the Opera House and Harbour Bridge offers the city's most iconic views, perfect for first-time visitors and couples.

areas.name: Sydney CBD
areas.why: The central business district offers high-rise luxury hotels with skyline and harbor views, fine-dining restaurants and designer shopping, ideal for those who want convenience.

areas.name: Double Bay
areas.why: This upscale harbor-side suburb in the eastern suburbs features chic boutiques and cafés, suited to travelers who want a quieter, residential feel within reach of the beaches.

themes.anniversary: Celebrate an anniversary in Sydney with a harbor-view suite at The Rocks or Circular Quay, where the Opera House sails and the Harbour Bridge fill the windows. Book a tasting menu at one of the city's acclaimed restaurants, take in a performance at the Opera House, and climb the Harbour Bridge together at twilight. Spend a day in the Hunter Valley wine region, a couple of hours north, then return for cocktails on the water as the ferries criss-cross the harbor.
themes.ultra: Sydney's finest suites are defined by a single view: the Opera House and Harbour Bridge framed from a private terrace, ideally from a high floor around Circular Quay. Personal butlers, private yacht charters on the harbor and seaplane flights to the Northern Beaches or a waterside lunch on Pittwater are the signature extras. Few cities place their most famous landmarks so close to the best rooms, and the premium here is paid for that front-row perspective.

bora-bora.overview: Bora Bora is the definitive overwater bungalow destination, a volcanic island ringed by a vivid turquoise lagoon and a necklace of motus, with Mount Otemanu rising above it all. Luxury here is about privacy, water and silence: villas with glass floor panels, private decks, plunge pools and direct lagoon access, with service delivered by outrigger canoe.
bora-bora.bestTime: May through October is the dry season, with lower humidity, steady trade winds and pleasant temperatures. November through April is warmer and wetter, with occasional heavy rain, but the lagoon stays inviting year-round.

areas.name: Eastern motus
areas.why: The islets on the eastern side of the lagoon face Mount Otemanu across calm, shallow water, offering the most iconic views and the greatest seclusion.

areas.name: Matira Point
areas.why: At the southern tip of the main island, Matira Beach is one of the island's finest stretches of white sand, ideal for those who want easy access to restaurants and island life.

areas.name: Northern and western motus
areas.why: Closer to the airport motu, these islets offer sunset views over the open ocean and the neighboring islands, suited to travelers who want convenience and evening light.

themes.honeymoon: Bora Bora is the ultimate honeymoon destination, and the overwater villa is the centerpiece. Choose a bungalow with a private plunge pool and a deck facing Mount Otemanu on the eastern motus, and arrange breakfast delivered by canoe. Snorkel with rays and reef sharks in the lagoon, take a private boat to a deserted motu for a picnic, and end each day watching the sunset from your own deck in total privacy.
themes.anniversary: For an anniversary, combine Bora Bora's natural beauty with a sense of occasion. Book a premium overwater villa or beachfront suite, and arrange a private dinner set up on a sandbank in the lagoon, with flowers and Polynesian music. Spend a day on a 4x4 tour up the main island's ridges for views over the lagoon, take a sunset cruise past Mount Otemanu and enjoy couples' treatments together in a spa set above the water.
themes.ultra: Bora Bora's pinnacle is the multi-bedroom villa, either perched over the lagoon or set on its own stretch of beach, with large infinity pools, private gardens and a dedicated butler. Private boat transfers from the airport motu, in-villa dining, personal chefs and excursions to uninhabited motus are part of the arrangement. The most prized of these residences face Mount Otemanu across the water, and there are only a handful of them on the entire lagoon.
